observations: The exact newly built indexed worker queried one group while disabled using a fresh bearer token and the installed source query parameters. The group result appeared once on the standard data-page endpoint.

After enabling the worker, a real HTTP AES-CBC callback with signature headers and no verification token granted the configured administrator a native site disable. Its processing reaction and exact cleanup used the active token. A separately signed non-administrator received the source denial. An unsigned encrypted administrator command did not alter the site.

The next group lookup used a third temporary bearer and saved a safe numeric provider rejection without the provider message. An actual subsequent Lark message still used the unchanged warm active token. A malformed group response used its own fourth token and saved an empty failure. Both result cards were consumed once.
